title: Irregular Verbs
sourceNote: The auto-captions are heavily garbled; the verb forms are standard German, but the exercise sentences at the end were reconstructed from context.
objectives: I can explain what an irregular verb is
I can recognise the vowel changes e → i, e → ie, a → ä and au → äu
I can conjugate the most important irregular verbs for A1
I can use these verbs correctly with du and er / sie / es

expressions.en: Do you speak German and Spanish?

patterns.form: Irregular verb: vowel changes only with du and er / sie / es
patterns.ex: ich spreche, du sprichst, er spricht
patterns.en: I speak, you speak, he speaks

grammar.title: What is different in irregular verbs?
grammar.body: In irregular verbs (*unregelmäßige* or *starke Verben*) the stem vowel changes, but **only with du and er / sie / es**. All other forms (*ich, wir, ihr, sie / Sie*) are formed like regular verbs. The endings do not change: *-e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en*.
grammar.ar: التغيير في حرف العلّة يحدث فقط مع du و er/sie/es.

grammar.title: The four vowel changes
grammar.body:
Learn the verbs in groups. The vowel changes are:

**e → i**: sprechen, nehmen, treffen, essen
**e → ie**: lesen, sehen
**a → ä**: fahren, waschen
**au → äu**: laufen

The verb *nehmen* is an exception: besides the vowel change, the consonant changes too (*du nimmst*, *er nimmt*).

grammar.title: e → ie: lesen, sehen
grammar.body: Here the short *e* becomes a long *ie*.

grammar.title: a → ä and au → äu
grammar.body: The vowels *a* and *au* get an umlaut with *du* and *er / sie / es*.

grammar.title: A special verb: wissen
grammar.body: *Wissen* (to know a fact) is special: the vowel changes in the singular, **including ich**. The *ich* and *er / sie / es* forms have no ending.

mistakes.why: *sprechen* changes e → i with *er / sie / es*.
With *ich* there is no vowel change.

pronunciation.tip: In *liest* and *siehst* the *ie* is one long *ee* sound, like 'lee-st'.

lines.de: Ja, ich fahre nach Berlin. Ich treffe Sabine.
lines.en: Yes, I am going to Berlin. I am meeting Sabine.

lines.de: Sabine? Sie liest immer ein Buch!
lines.en: Sabine? She is always reading a book!

lines.de: Ja! Und sie spricht Deutsch und Spanisch.
lines.en: Yes! And she speaks German and Spanish.

tip: Learn irregular verbs with their du-form and er-form together: sprechen – du sprichst – er spricht.

comprehension.q: With which pronouns does the stem vowel change?
comprehension.a: Only with du and er / sie / es.

comprehension.q: Which verb is special because even *ich* has a changed form?

summary: Irregular verbs change the stem vowel only with du and er / sie / es.
Changes: e → i (sprechen, nehmen, treffen, essen), e → ie (lesen, sehen), a → ä (fahren, waschen), au → äu (laufen).
The endings are the same as for regular verbs.
nehmen: du nimmst, er nimmt; wissen: ich weiß, du weißt, er weiß.
